generations.memory_31: Signup simplification is a validated lever for SMB: signup rose 15%, activation 9%, and qualified revenue 4%. Retention dipped 1%, so keep this scoped to SMB until tested elsewhere.
generations.memory_44: The sales-assisted CTA works for enterprise prospects: qualified leads increased 24% and qualified revenue 18%, despite a 12% signup decline. No retention change was observed; do not extend this conclusion beyond enterprise.
generations.memory_57: Referral incentives performed well in established accounts, increasing referral starts 21%, qualified revenue 7%, and 30-day retention 2%. The effect was concentrated in accounts more than six months old.
generations.memory_73: The targeted 40% discount drove strong acquisition—signups up 31% and qualified revenue up 18%—but 30-day retention fell 12%. The cohort fails to hold through the first renewal cycle, so do not treat broad discounting as a sustainable growth strategy.
generations.memory_86: Shortening onboarding is a confirmed improvement: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%.
generations.memory_91: In-product activation messaging produced modest but consistent gains: week-one engagement increased 11%, activation 6%, and 30-day retention 1%. The experiment is confirmed.
